# Course overview {.unnumbered}

::: {.course-intro}
::: {.course-tag}
Topic Course · Independent study
:::

**Generative AI through the lens of statisticians**

A personal learning course by [Chi-Kuang Yeh](https://chikuang.github.io/): starting with a background in statistics and statistical machine learning, and building an understanding of attention, transformers, generative models, and AI agents from the ground up.
:::

## Who this course is for

The starting point is a statistician who is comfortable with probability, inference, linear algebra, optimization, and statistical machine learning, but is new to modern generative AI and agent systems. Prior knowledge of deep learning, Python, or agent frameworks is not assumed. Python is introduced as we need it.

This is a **self-paced Topic Course** for independent study. It has no fixed semester, enrollment, examinations, or grading. The course language is English, with standard terminology that can be reused in teaching and research.

## The learning path

:::: {.course-path}
::: {}
### 01 · Understand the model
Move from likelihood and feature maps to tokens, embeddings, attention, and transformers.
:::
::: {}
### 02 · Understand generation
Study conditional sampling, latent variables, diffusion, adaptation, and retrieval.
:::
::: {}
### 03 · Understand the system
Evaluate uncertainty, build tool-using agents, and design reproducible experiments.
:::
::::

## Start here

1. Read the [course outline](syllabus.qmd): 14 ordered modules with learning goals, statistical connections, and Python practice.
2. Keep the [statistical lens](statistical-lens.qmd) nearby as a translation guide.
3. Set up [Python + Quarto](python-workflow.qmd), then run the [first Python lab](01-python-lab.qmd).
4. Use the [reading guide](readings.qmd) for selected book sections, official tutorials, and foundational papers.

## What I want to be able to do

- Explain an LLM as a conditional probability model, including its training objective and sampling procedure.
- Derive and implement a small attention mechanism, and explain how it fits inside a transformer.
- Compare autoregressive, latent-variable, and diffusion approaches to generation.
- Distinguish prompting, retrieval, fine-tuning, and preference optimization by what each changes.
- Build a small agent that calls tools, observes results, and knows when to stop.
- Evaluate a GenAI system using explicit targets, held-out tasks, baselines, uncertainty estimates, and error analysis.

## How we will learn

Each module follows the same sequence: **a concrete question → a statistical formulation → a small Python experiment → an explanation in plain language**. NumPy makes the mathematics visible; PyTorch is introduced for automatic differentiation and neural networks. Small examples come before large pretrained models.

::: {.callout-note title="Current course materials"}
The outline, statistical connections, Python authoring guide, reading list, and first executable lab are available. The 14 modules describe the planned learning sequence; complete lecture notes and additional labs will be developed progressively.
:::
